using LinearAlgebra
using Printf
using Random

# The rod's centres of n equal cells on [0, 1], and the true initial temperature
# (made up): a smooth hump, a hot block and a fine ripple, on 20 degrees.
function true_profile(n)
    x = [(j - 0.5) / n for j in 1:n]
    hump(x) = 35 * exp(-((x - 0.2) / 0.06)^2)
    block(x) = 0.42 <= x <= 0.56 ? 25.0 : 0.0
    ripple(x) = 0.68 <= x <= 0.92 ? 12 * sin(2pi * (x - 0.68) / 0.08) : 0.0
    return x, [20 + hump(a) + block(a) + ripple(a) for a in x]
end

# The rod's finite differences with insulated ends form a symmetric matrix L, so
# A = exp(-alpha T L) = V diag(s) V', and s are its singular values, largest first.
function heat_modes(n, alpha, T)
    h = 1 / n
    diagonal = fill(2.0, n)
    diagonal[1] = diagonal[n] = 1.0
    F = eigen(SymTridiagonal(diagonal ./ h^2, fill(-1.0 / h^2, n - 1)))
    return F.vectors, exp.(-alpha * T .* max.(F.values, 0.0))
end

function main(inputs, report)
    outputs = Dict{String,Any}()
    s = Tsugumi.input(inputs, "settings")
    n, alpha, T, noise = Int(s["cells"]), s["alpha"], s["final_time"], s["noise"]
    x, truth = true_profile(n)
    V, sigma = heat_modes(n, alpha, T)
    clean = V * (sigma .* (V' * truth))
    rng = Xoshiro(s["seed"])
    measured = clean .+ noise .* randn(rng, n)

    heat_change = (sum(clean) - sum(truth)) / sum(truth)
    abs(heat_change) < 1e-10 || error("insulated ends must keep the heat: relative change $heat_change")
    report.log(string(@sprintf("relative change of the total heat: %.2e", heat_change)))

    outputs["measurement"] = Dict("seed" => s["seed"], "alpha" => alpha, "final_time" => T, "noise" => noise,
                                    "x" => x, "truth" => truth, "measured" => measured)
    round3(v) = round(v; digits=3)
    lines = [Dict("x" => x[j], "u" => round3(series[j]), "line" => name)
             for (name, series) in (("Initial temperature (true, made up)", truth), ("Temperature at time T", clean)) for j in 1:n]
    points = [Dict("x" => x[j], "u" => round3(measured[j])) for j in 1:n]
    report.vegalite(Dict(
        "\$schema" => "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json",
        "background" => "white",
        "title" => Dict("anchor" => "start", "text" => @sprintf("Heat loses its details first: measured at T = %g (noise %g °C)", T, noise),
                        "subtitle" => @sprintf("A made-up rod. Both ends are insulated; the relative change in total heat is %.1e", heat_change)),
        "usermeta" => Dict("x" => x, "truth" => truth, "clean" => clean, "measured" => measured, "heat_change" => heat_change),
        "layer" => [
            Dict("data" => Dict("values" => lines), "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "strokeWidth" => 2),
                 "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "x", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Position along the rod x"),
                                    "y" => Dict("field" => "u", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Temperature (°C)"),
                                    "color" => Dict("field" => "line", "type" => "nominal", "title" => nothing,
                                                    "scale" => Dict("domain" => ["Initial temperature (true, made up)", "Temperature at time T", "Measurements"], "range" => ["#111111", "#eb6834", "#2a78d6"]),
                                                    "legend" => Dict("orient" => "top-right")))),
            Dict("data" => Dict("values" => points), "mark" => Dict("type" => "point", "filled" => true, "size" => 16, "color" => "#2a78d6"),
                 "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "x", "type" => "quantitative"), "y" => Dict("field" => "u", "type" => "quantitative"),
                                    "color" => Dict("datum" => "Measurements"))),
        ]))

    return outputs
end

using LinearAlgebra
using Printf

# The rod's finite differences with insulated ends form a symmetric matrix L, so
# A = exp(-alpha T L) = V diag(s) V', and s are its singular values, largest first.
function heat_modes(n, alpha, T)
    h = 1 / n
    diagonal = fill(2.0, n)
    diagonal[1] = diagonal[n] = 1.0
    F = eigen(SymTridiagonal(diagonal ./ h^2, fill(-1.0 / h^2, n - 1)))
    return F.vectors, exp.(-alpha * T .* max.(F.values, 0.0))

# Why it is ill-posed: the singular values fall steeply, and all modes whose
# signal is under the noise are lost to any inversion.
function main(inputs, report)
    m = Tsugumi.input(inputs, "measurement")
    x, truth, measured = Float64.(m["x"]), Float64.(m["truth"]), Float64.(m["measured"])
    alpha, T, noise = m["alpha"], m["final_time"], m["noise"]
    n = length(x)
    factors = Float64.(inputs.params["time_factors"])

    smallest = 1e-30 # below this the chart stops
    decay = Dict{String,Any}[]
    labels = String[]
    for f in factors
        label = @sprintf("T = %g", f * T)
        push!(labels, label)
        _, s = heat_modes(n, alpha, f * T)
        for k in 1:n
            s[k] > smallest && push!(decay, Dict("k" => k, "sigma" => s[k], "time" => label))
        end
    end

    # The Picard picture at this T: the data along each mode, against the signal.
    V, s = heat_modes(n, alpha, T)
    signal = abs.(s .* (V' * truth))
    seen = abs.(V' * measured)
    resolved = noise > 0 ? count(signal .> noise) : n
    report.log(string(@sprintf("modes with a signal above the noise at T = %g: %d of %d; sigma_1 = %.3g, sigma_%d = %.3g", T, resolved, n, s[1], n, s[n])))
    floor_value = 1e-6
    picard = [Dict("k" => k, "v" => v[k], "series" => name)
              for (name, v) in (("Signal left by the initial temperature", signal), ("Components in the measurement", seen)) for k in 1:n if v[k] >= floor_value]

    report.vegalite(Dict(
        "\$schema" => "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json",
        "background" => "white",
        "title" => Dict("text" => @sprintf("Singular values drop sharply: %d of %d modes stay above the noise", resolved, n),
                        "subtitle" => "Left: the later, the faster they fall. Right: once the measurement's components level off at the height of the noise (orange line), what lies beyond cannot be recovered"),
        "usermeta" => Dict("singular_values" => s, "resolved" => resolved),
        "resolve" => Dict("scale" => Dict("color" => "independent")),
        "hconcat" => [
            Dict("width" => 310, "height" => 240, "data" => Dict("values" => decay),
                 "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "strokeWidth" => 2),
                 "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "k", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Mode number k"),
                                    "y" => Dict("field" => "sigma", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Singular value",
                                                "scale" => Dict("type" => "log", "domain" => [smallest, 1.5], "nice" => false),
                                                "axis" => Dict("values" => [1e-30, 1e-20, 1e-10, 1], "format" => ".0e")),
                                    "color" => Dict("field" => "time", "type" => "nominal", "title" => "Measurement time", "sort" => labels,
                                                    "scale" => Dict("range" => ["#1baf7a", "#2a78d6", "#eda100"]),
                                                    "legend" => Dict("orient" => "bottom-left")))),
            Dict("width" => 310, "height" => 240,
                 "layer" => [
                     Dict("data" => Dict("values" => picard), "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "strokeWidth" => 1.6),
                          "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "k", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Mode number k"),
                                             "y" => Dict("field" => "v", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Size of the component (°C)",
                                                         "scale" => Dict("type" => "log", "domain" => [floor_value, 1e3], "nice" => false),
                                                         "axis" => Dict("values" => [1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-2, 1, 100], "format" => "~g")),
                                             "color" => Dict("field" => "series", "type" => "nominal", "title" => nothing,
                                                             "scale" => Dict("range" => ["#111111", "#2a78d6"], "domain" => ["Signal left by the initial temperature", "Components in the measurement"]),
                                                             "legend" => Dict("orient" => "top-right")))),
                     Dict("data" => Dict("values" => [Dict("v" => max(noise, floor_value))]), "mark" => Dict("type" => "rule", "color" => "#eb6834", "strokeDash" => [5, 3], "strokeWidth" => 2),
                          "encoding" => Dict("y" => Dict("field" => "v", "type" => "quantitative"))),
                 ]),
        ]))

    return nothing
end

# Dividing by the singular values: the noise (or even round-off) along the
# smallest ones is multiplied by 1 / sigma. The values are limited only so that
# they stay representable.
function main(inputs, report)
    m = Tsugumi.input(inputs, "measurement")
    x, truth, measured = Float64.(m["x"]), Float64.(m["truth"]), Float64.(m["measured"])
    n = length(x)
    V, s = heat_modes(n, m["alpha"], m["final_time"])
    gain = 1 ./ max.(s, 1e-290)
    invert(d) = clamp.(V * (gain .* (V' * d)), -1e300, 1e300)
    from_measured = invert(measured)
    from_clean = invert(V * (s .* (V' * truth)))
    peak = maximum(abs, from_measured)
    peak_clean = maximum(abs, from_clean)
    report.log(string(@sprintf("largest |u0| from the measured data %.3g, from noise-free data (round-off only) %.3g; truth %.3g", peak, peak_clean, maximum(abs, truth))))

    rows = [Dict("x" => x[j], "u" => series[j], "line" => name)
            for (name, series) in (("Naive inverse (from measurements)", from_measured), ("Naive inverse (without noise)", from_clean), ("True initial temperature", truth)) for j in 1:n]
    report.vegalite(Dict(
        "\$schema" => "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json",
        "background" => "white",
        "title" => Dict("anchor" => "start", "text" => @sprintf("Solving the inverse naively diverges: up to %.1e °C", peak),
                        "subtitle" => @sprintf("A⁻¹ d computed as it is (the truth peaks at %.0f °C; symmetric log axis). Even without noise, rounding alone gives %.1e °C", maximum(truth), peak_clean)),
        "usermeta" => Dict("peak" => peak, "peak_clean" => peak_clean, "smallest_singular_value" => s[end]),
        "data" => Dict("values" => rows),
        "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "strokeWidth" => 1.4),
        "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "x", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Position along the rod x"),
                           "y" => Dict("field" => "u", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Estimated initial temperature (°C)",
                                       "scale" => Dict("type" => "symlog", "constant" => 100.0),
                                       "axis" => Dict("format" => ".0e", "values" => [-1e30, -1e20, -1e10, 0, 1e10, 1e20, 1e30])),
                           "color" => Dict("field" => "line", "type" => "nominal", "title" => nothing,
                                           "scale" => Dict("domain" => ["Naive inverse (from measurements)", "Naive inverse (without noise)", "True initial temperature"], "range" => ["#2a78d6", "#eda100", "#111111"]),

using LinearAlgebra
using Printf

# The rod's finite differences with insulated ends form a symmetric matrix L, so
# A = exp(-alpha T L) = V diag(s) V', and s are its singular values, largest first.
function heat_modes(n, alpha, T)
    h = 1 / n
    diagonal = fill(2.0, n)
    diagonal[1] = diagonal[n] = 1.0
    F = eigen(SymTridiagonal(diagonal ./ h^2, fill(-1.0 / h^2, n - 1)))
    return F.vectors, exp.(-alpha * T .* max.(F.values, 0.0))
end

# The corner of the L-curve: where log(norm) against log(residual) bends most,
# by the finite-difference curvature along the sweep.
function corner(log_residual, log_norm)
    best, at = -Inf, 2
    for i in 2:length(log_norm)-1
        dx1, dy1 = log_residual[i] - log_residual[i - 1], log_norm[i] - log_norm[i - 1]
        dx2, dy2 = log_residual[i + 1] - log_residual[i], log_norm[i + 1] - log_norm[i]
        curvature = 2 * (dx1 * dy2 - dx2 * dy1) / (hypot(dx1, dy1) * hypot(dx2, dy2) * hypot(dx1 + dx2, dy1 + dy2) + 1e-300)
        if curvature > best
            best, at = curvature, i
        end
    end
    return at
end

# Tikhonov: minimize |A u - d|^2 + lambda^2 |u|^2, which damps each mode by the
# filter sigma / (sigma^2 + lambda^2). Three ways to choose lambda are compared.
function main(inputs, report)
    outputs = Dict{String,Any}()
    m = Tsugumi.input(inputs, "measurement")
    x, truth, measured = Float64.(m["x"]), Float64.(m["truth"]), Float64.(m["measured"])
    n = length(x)
    noise = m["noise"]
    lambdas = exp10.(range(inputs.params["log10_lambda_min"], inputs.params["log10_lambda_max"]; length=Int(inputs.params["sweep"])))
    V, s = heat_modes(n, m["alpha"], m["final_time"])
    coefficients = V' * measured

    solve(l) = V * ((s ./ (s .^ 2 .+ l^2)) .* coefficients)
    residual(u) = norm(V * (s .* (V' * u)) - measured)
    rms(v) = sqrt(sum(abs2, v) / length(v))
    solutions = [solve(l) for l in lambdas]
    residuals = residual.(solutions)
    norms = norm.(solutions)
    errors = [rms(u - truth) for u in solutions]

    # Discrepancy principle: the largest lambda that fits the data down to the noise.
    target = noise * sqrt(n)
    candidates = findall(<=(target), residuals)
    discrepancy = isempty(candidates) ? 1 : maximum(candidates)
    lcurve = corner(log.(residuals), log.(norms))
    oracle = argmin(errors)

    describe_choice(name, i) = report.log(string(@sprintf("%s: lambda %.3g, RMS error %.3f, residual %.3f", name, lambdas[i], errors[i], residuals[i])))
    describe_choice("discrepancy", discrepancy)
    describe_choice("L-curve", lcurve)
    describe_choice("best against the truth", oracle)
    outputs["choice"] = Dict("discrepancy" => lambdas[discrepancy], "lcurve" => lambdas[lcurve], "oracle" => lambdas[oracle],
                               "error_discrepancy" => errors[discrepancy], "error_lcurve" => errors[lcurve], "error_oracle" => errors[oracle])

    sweep = [Dict("lambda" => lambdas[i], "residual" => residuals[i], "norm" => norms[i], "error" => errors[i]) for i in eachindex(lambdas)]
    marks = [Dict("lambda" => lambdas[i], "residual" => residuals[i], "norm" => norms[i], "error" => errors[i], "method" => name)
             for (name, i) in (("Discrepancy principle", discrepancy), ("Corner of the L", lcurve), ("Closest to the truth", oracle))]
    method = Dict("field" => "method", "type" => "nominal", "title" => "How λ is chosen",
                  "scale" => Dict("domain" => ["Discrepancy principle", "Corner of the L", "Closest to the truth"], "range" => ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"]))
    mark_point = Dict("type" => "point", "filled" => true, "size" => 110, "stroke" => "white", "strokeWidth" => 1.5, "opacity" => 1)
    lambda_axis = Dict("field" => "lambda", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Strength of regularisation λ", "scale" => Dict("type" => "log"), "axis" => Dict("format" => ".0e", "tickCount" => 5))
    log_x = Dict("field" => "residual", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Residual ‖Au − d‖", "scale" => Dict("type" => "log", "nice" => false, "zero" => false), "axis" => Dict("format" => "~g", "tickCount" => 5, "grid" => false))
    log_y = Dict("field" => "norm", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Size of the solution ‖u‖", "scale" => Dict("type" => "log", "nice" => false, "zero" => false), "axis" => Dict("format" => "~g", "tickCount" => 5, "grid" => false))
    y_error = Dict("field" => "error", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "RMS error against the truth (°C)", "scale" => Dict("type" => "log", "nice" => false), "axis" => Dict("format" => "~g", "tickCount" => 5, "grid" => false))

    report.vegalite(Dict(

        "background" => "white",
        "title" => Dict("text" => @sprintf("The trade-off of λ: by the discrepancy principle λ = %.2g, error %.2f °C", lambdas[discrepancy], errors[discrepancy]),
                        "subtitle" => @sprintf("At the corner of the L, λ = %.2g (error %.2f °C). Knowing the truth, λ = %.2g (error %.2f °C)", lambdas[lcurve], errors[lcurve], lambdas[oracle], errors[oracle])),

using LinearAlgebra
using Printf
using Random

# The rod's finite differences with insulated ends form a symmetric matrix L, so
# A = exp(-alpha T L) = V diag(s) V', and s are its singular values, largest first.
function heat_modes(n, alpha, T)
    h = 1 / n
    diagonal = fill(2.0, n)
    diagonal[1] = diagonal[n] = 1.0
    F = eigen(SymTridiagonal(diagonal ./ h^2, fill(-1.0 / h^2, n - 1)))
    return F.vectors, exp.(-alpha * T .* max.(F.values, 0.0))
end

# The same rod and the same noise, measured later and later: each time lambda is
# set by the discrepancy principle. Waiting loses detail that no method brings back.
function main(inputs, report)
    m = Tsugumi.input(inputs, "measurement")
    x, truth = Float64.(m["x"]), Float64.(m["truth"])
    n = length(x)
    noise = m["noise"]
    times = sort(Float64.(inputs.params["times"]))
    lambdas = exp10.(range(-8, 2; length=121))
    rng = Xoshiro(m["seed"] + 1)
    rms(v) = sqrt(sum(abs2, v) / length(v))

    labels = String[]
    errors = Float64[]
    chosen = Float64[]
    modes = Int[]
    rows = Dict{String,Any}[]
    for T in times
        V, s = heat_modes(n, m["alpha"], T)
        clean = V * (s .* (V' * truth))
        measured = clean .+ noise .* randn(rng, n)
        coefficients = V' * measured
        solve(l) = V * ((s ./ (s .^ 2 .+ l^2)) .* coefficients)
        fits = findall(l -> norm(V * (s .* (V' * solve(l))) - measured) <= noise * sqrt(n), lambdas)
        l = isempty(fits) ? lambdas[1] : lambdas[maximum(fits)]
        u = solve(l)
        push!(errors, rms(u - truth))
        push!(chosen, l)
        push!(modes, count(abs.(V' * clean) .> noise))
        label = @sprintf("T = %g (error %.1f °C)", T, errors[end])
        push!(labels, label)
        append!(rows, [Dict("x" => x[j], "u" => round(u[j]; digits=3), "panel" => label) for j in 1:n])
        append!(rows, [Dict("x" => x[j], "truth" => truth[j], "panel" => label) for j in 1:n])
        report.log(string(@sprintf("T = %g: lambda %.3g, RMS error %.3f, %d modes above the noise", T, l, errors[end], modes[end])))
    end
    summary = [Dict("T" => times[i], "error" => errors[i], "modes" => modes[i]) for i in eachindex(times)]

    report.vegalite(Dict(
        "\$schema" => "https://vega.github.io/schema/vega-lite/v6.json",
        "background" => "white",
        "title" => Dict("text" => "The later you measure, the more detail is lost",
                        "subtitle" => @sprintf("The same rod measured with noise %g °C. Black: truth (made up); blue: recovered. Below: the recovery's error, and the number of modes left above the noise", noise)),
        "usermeta" => Dict("times" => times, "errors" => errors, "lambdas" => chosen, "modes" => modes),
        "vconcat" => [
            Dict("data" => Dict("values" => rows),
                 "facet" => Dict("field" => "panel", "type" => "nominal", "sort" => labels, "title" => nothing, "header" => Dict("labelFontSize" => 11)),
                 "columns" => 3,
                 "spec" => Dict("width" => 235, "height" => 130,
                                "layer" => [
                                    Dict("transform" => [Dict("filter" => "isValid(datum.truth)")], "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "color" => "#111111", "strokeWidth" => 1.4),
                                         "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "x", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Position along the rod x"),
                                                            "y" => Dict("field" => "truth", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Initial temperature (°C)"))),
                                    Dict("transform" => [Dict("filter" => "isValid(datum.u)")], "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "color" => "#2a78d6", "strokeWidth" => 1.6),
                                         "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "x", "type" => "quantitative"), "y" => Dict("field" => "u", "type" => "quantitative"))),
                                ])),
            Dict("hconcat" => [
                Dict("width" => 350, "height" => 110, "data" => Dict("values" => summary), "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "point" => true, "color" => "#eb6834", "strokeWidth" => 2),
                     "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "T", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Measurement time T", "scale" => Dict("type" => "log"), "axis" => Dict("format" => "~g", "tickCount" => 4, "grid" => false)),
                                        "y" => Dict("field" => "error", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "RMS error (°C)"))),
                Dict("width" => 350, "height" => 110, "data" => Dict("values" => summary), "mark" => Dict("type" => "line", "point" => true, "color" => "#2a78d6", "strokeWidth" => 2),
                     "encoding" => Dict("x" => Dict("field" => "T", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Measurement time T", "scale" => Dict("type" => "log"), "axis" => Dict("format" => "~g", "tickCount" => 4, "grid" => false)),
                                        "y" => Dict("field" => "modes", "type" => "quantitative", "title" => "Modes left"))),
            ]),
        ]))

    return nothing
end

using LinearAlgebra
using Printf

# The rod's finite differences with insulated ends form a symmetric matrix L, so
# A = exp(-alpha T L) = V diag(s) V', and s are its singular values, largest first.
function heat_modes(n, alpha, T)
    h = 1 / n
    diagonal = fill(2.0, n)
    diagonal[1] = diagonal[n] = 1.0
    F = eigen(SymTridiagonal(diagonal ./ h^2, fill(-1.0 / h^2, n - 1)))
    return F.vectors, exp.(-alpha * T .* max.(F.values, 0.0))
end

# Each check has a known answer, independent of the noise in this run.
function main(inputs, report)
    m = Tsugumi.input(inputs, "measurement")
    x, truth = Float64.(m["x"]), Float64.(m["truth"])
    n = length(x)
    alpha, T = m["alpha"], m["final_time"]
    V, s = heat_modes(n, alpha, T)
    forward(u) = V * (s .* (V' * u))
    rows = Vector{Any}[]
    function require(name, value, limit, text)
        value <= limit || error(@sprintf("%s: %.3e is above %.1e", name, value, limit))
        push!(rows, [name, text, @sprintf("%.2e", value), @sprintf("%.0e", limit)])
    end

    # 1. Insulated ends keep the total heat.
    change = abs(sum(forward(truth)) - sum(truth)) / sum(truth)
    require("Total heat is conserved", change, 1e-10, "relative change")

    # 2. A cosine is an exact mode of the rod: it decays by the analytic factor.
    k = 3
    mode = cos.(k * pi .* x)
    continuous = exp(-alpha * (k * pi)^2 * T)
    discrete = exp(-alpha * 4 * n^2 * sin(k * pi / (2n))^2 * T)
    decay_error = maximum(abs, forward(mode) - discrete * mode)
    require("cos(3πx) decays at the discrete rate", decay_error, 1e-10, @sprintf("difference from the factor %.6f", discrete))
    require("The discrete decay rate is close to the continuous solution", abs(discrete - continuous) / continuous, 0.01, @sprintf("relative difference from the continuous factor %.6f", continuous))

    # 3. The eigendecomposition agrees with small implicit time steps.
    steps = 2000
    dt = T / steps
    h = 1 / n
    d = fill(2.0, n)
    d[1] = d[n] = 1.0
    B = I + alpha * dt * SymTridiagonal(d ./ h^2, fill(-1.0 / h^2, n - 1))
    u = copy(truth)
    for _ in 1:steps
        u = B \ u
    end
    require("Agrees with implicit time integration ($(steps) steps)", maximum(abs, u - forward(truth)), 0.05, "largest difference (°C)")

    # 4. Without noise, and early enough, the inversion recovers the truth.
    early = inputs.params["early_time"]
    W, e = heat_modes(n, alpha, early)
    clean = W * (e .* (W' * truth))
    recovered = W * ((e ./ (e .^ 2 .+ 1e-14)) .* (W' * clean))
    recovery = sqrt(sum(abs2, recovered - truth) / n)
    require(@sprintf("Recovery without noise at an early time T = %g", early), recovery, 1e-6, @sprintf("RMS error (°C), smallest singular value %.3f", e[end]))

    # 5. Heat flows down the gradient: the extremes only move inward.
    clean_later = forward(truth)
    spread = (maximum(clean_later) <= maximum(truth) + 1e-9 && minimum(clean_later) >= minimum(truth) - 1e-9) ? 0.0 : 1.0
    require("Never beyond the highest and lowest temperatures (maximum principle)", spread, 0.0, "any violation (0 = none)")

    report.table(["Checked", "What the value is", "Value", "Tolerance"], rows)

    return nothing
end

notes.html:
An inverse problem in heat conduction

The problem of finding a rod's initial temperature from its temperature at a later time. The data is made up, with random noise added.

ut=αuxx,u(x,T)=∑ke−αλkT⟨u0,ϕk⟩ϕku_t=\alpha u_{xx},\quad u(x,T)=\sum_k e^{-\alpha\lambda_k T}\langle u_0,\phi_k\rangle\phi_k

The finer a mode, the faster it vanishes as e−αλkTe^{-\alpha\lambda_k T}, so solving backwards amplifies the noise by the same factor (naive). Tikhonov regularisation damps the components of small singular values.

min⁡u ∥Au−d∥2+λ2∥u∥2,u^=∑kσkσk2+λ2(ukTd) vk\min_u\ \|Au-d\|^2+\lambda^2\|u\|^2,\quad \hat u=\sum_k\frac{\sigma_k}{\sigma_k^2+\lambda^2}(u_k^{\mathsf T}d)\,v_k

λ\lambda is chosen by the discrepancy principle ∥Au^−d∥≈σnoisen\|A\hat u-d\|\approx\sigma_{\rm noise}\sqrt{n} or at the corner of the L-curve (tikhonov). The "closest λ\lambda", which needs the truth, is only for comparison.

Try final_time and noise of settings, and lambda of reconstruct. horizon shows the details lost by measuring late.

The size of the noise is taken as known. On this grid the vanished modes cannot be recovered, and the recovery is "one solution consistent with the measurements".
